newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Hungary inflation to ease slowly-central bank head.
newsitem.headline: Hungary inflation to ease slowly-central bank head.

text.p: Hungary's inflation rate will ease to around 17 percent by year-end but will unlikely fall to single-digit levels before the turn of the century, Hungarian central bank chief Gyorgy Suranyi said on Wednesday
"The end-year target is around 17 percent," Suranyi told reporters during an economic conference in Vienna. At the end of last year, inflation stood at 19.8 percent, he added.
Suranyi said inflation should slow further in 1998, but he declined to give a specific target. "Probably in 1998, there will be a chance for an even faster slowdown," he said.
The central bank chief attributed the relatively slow pace of disinflation to a more than 20-percent increase in energy prices at the start of this year.
"The price adjustment was necessary but had a temporary negative effect on inflation," he said. "We're going to complete all important price adjustments this year."

But Suranyi warned that Hungary, seen as one of the frontrunners for early membership in the European Union, could not reduce its inflation rate to single-digit levels until its transition to a fully-western style economy was completed.
"It is absolutely impossible to achieve single-digit inflation as long as economic transition is not completed," he told the conference earlier.
"That doesnt mean we shouldnt bring inflation down as fast as possible, but forceful moves cannot be fruitful," he added.
Suranyi said he hoped the country's inflation rate could be pushed below 10 percent "in two to three years."
The central bank chief added that Hungary had no plans to tap the Eurobond market in the near future.
"We have no immediate plans to move to the Eurobond market in the next few months," he said. "We have no borrowing needs in the current year." -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom =431 53112 274
